justification: Standard: a new validation layer added to scripts/qa_gate.py, which runs on every single PR unconditionally -- this changes what every future Standard/Critical PR touching services/ or scripts/ is required to prove. Not Critical: purely additive to the gate itself (a new required field/check, opt-out via an explicit written exemption, never a change to how existing checks behave). Not Minor: it changes enforcement behaviour for every future PR, not a documentation or wording change.

pre_impl.existing_data: Reuses changed_line_numbers() (already in qa_gate.py, used by the existing scanner layers) rather than reimplementing diff-line parsing a second time. Reads only files already present in the checkout (the changed .py file itself, and tests/test_<base>*.py candidates) -- no database, no network call, no new external dependency.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Originally assumed a function's own body text would contain the DB/HTTP call directly (matching services/drawdown_verify.py's mocked-test detector from earlier the same session). Forced this assumption to fail on purpose: hid the real test files for services/drawdown_verify.py and ran the new check against submit_drawdown_verify -- it reported ZERO findings, because that function delegates to a local helper (_insert_audit) which is the one that actually calls .execute(); the function itself never does. Fixed by resolving one level of same-file local calls (_ast_functions now tracks each function's local call names, check_real_layer_test_exists checks the function's own body OR any locally-called helper's body). Re-verified the same force-fail: now correctly reports 1 finding with files hidden, 0 with files present.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Applies to every future PR from merge onward. Does not retroactively require tests for existing DB/HTTP-touching files that are never touched again -- a file with no changed lines in a given PR is never scanned by this check, on purpose, matching every other diff-scoped layer in this file.
pre_impl.external_source_error: N/A -- this check itself makes no external call of any kind, by design (see the Layer 9.5 header comment: it is a static glob-and-AST check, not a test runner).
pre_impl.frontend_type: N/A -- Python-file scope only (services/, scripts/), matching where psycopg2/requests/httpx usage actually lives in this repo.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: N/A -- this is a CI/QA-gate check, not a user-facing code path.

falsifiable_check.command: python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); import qa_gate; ..." -- direct calls to check_real_layer_test_exists against services/drawdown_verify.py, with tests/test_drawdown_verify_real_db.py and tests/test_drawdown_verify_audit_failclosed.py renamed out of the way and back
falsifiable_check.fails_when: Run with the two real test files renamed to hide them from the tests/ glob, against the real, current services/drawdown_verify.py -- the exact file and function (submit_drawdown_verify) this session spent hours proving needed a real test.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: First attempt: 0 findings even with both real test files hidden -- a genuine bug, not the intended result. Root cause: submit_drawdown_verify calls the local helper _insert_audit() rather than touching psycopg2/.execute() directly, and the first version of this check only inspected each function's OWN body text, never functions it calls. Fixed (one level of local-call resolution added), re-run with files hidden: 'Real-layer test missing: services/drawdown_verify.py has a changed function that touches a database or HTTP call...' -- 1 finding, correctly. Files restored: 0 findings. Also checked: an explicit real_layer_exempt entry correctly suppresses the finding even with tests hidden, a file with zero DB/HTTP calls (services/da_outcome.py, services/upzoning_check.py -- confirmed by grep, 0 matches for psycopg2/.execute(/.cursor( in either) correctly produces zero findings, and the check generalises sensibly across other real files sampled cold (services/lot_search.py, services/solar_yield.py both correctly flagged their real DB/HTTP helper functions by different naming conventions than drawdown_verify.py's). All of this is now a permanent test file (tests/test_qa_gate_real_layer_requirement.py, 9 tests, including the exact real-file-hide/restore proof reproduced as TestAgainstTheRealFileThatMotivatedThis), not just an ad-hoc session script -- run: python -m pytest tests/test_qa_gate_real_layer_requirement.py -v, 9 passed.
falsifiable_check.round_2_sol_cross_review: An automated cross-reviewer (Sol) ran against the pushed commit and found 4 more real gaps, triaged: 2 fixed with new force-fail proof, 1 partially fixed (documented below), 1 named as an accepted limit rather than chased. (1) HIGH -- real_layer_exempt accepted membership alone: {"file": ""} or {"file": true} silently suppressed a finding with no actual reason written, contradicting this file own header comment (a written reason, not silent scope-cutting). FIXED: now requires the value to be a non-empty string after stripping. Force-fail proof: test_empty_or_non_string_exemption_is_rejected asserts empty string, whitespace-only, True, and None are all rejected (1 finding each) while a real string reason (existing test_explicit_exemption_suppresses_the_finding) still suppresses. (2) MEDIUM -- _REAL_LAYER_MARK_RE was an unanchored substring search, so it matched the marker text INSIDE A COMMENT (e.g. a comment saying it does not require the marker) as if it were real coverage. FIXED: anchored to the start of a logical line. First anchoring attempt was itself wrong -- it required pytest.mark. to start the line and broke both real tests, because this repo's actual convention is `pytestmark = pytest.mark.database` (an assignment, not a bare decorator) -- caught immediately by re-running this file own test suite against the real file, not assumed correct. Corrected to allow an optional @ or "pytestmark = " prefix; re-ran, 9/9 passed. (3) MEDIUM -- the HTTP trigger regex missed requests.Session()/httpx.Client() instance calls. PARTIALLY FIXED: added those two patterns. Deliberately NOT chased further -- aliased imports (from requests import post; post(url)) were considered and rejected, because a regex for a bare post(/get( call would false-positive on ordinary local functions with those names far more often than it would catch a real aliased call; named as an accepted gap rather than a fragile pattern. (4) MEDIUM -- by_name was a plain {name: fn} dict, so two same-named functions in different scopes (e.g. two classes each defining helper) silently collapsed to whichever one Python dict comprehension kept last; a call from the CHANGED function to the wrong-scope helper could read as no DB touch when the sibling with the same name does touch. FIXED: keyed to a list of all same-named definitions; a called name is now treated as touching if ANY of them touches directly -- erring toward requiring a test under ambiguity, per this file own never weaken when uncertain convention. Force-fail proof: test_duplicate_function_names_in_one_file_do_not_hide_a_db_touching_sibling, two classes each defining helper (one inert, one DB-touching), asserts the finding still fires. Full re-run after all four: python -m pytest tests/test_qa_gate_real_layer_requirement.py -v -- 11 passed (9 original + 2 new). python -m pytest tests/test_qa_gate*.py -q -- 72 passed, no regressions in the other 6 pre-existing qa_gate test files. Full python -m pytest -q -- 4967 passed, 2 skipped, 250 deselected, no failures.

functions.name: check_real_layer_test_exists
functions.input: report dict (for real_layer_exempt), diff_files (changed .py paths), project_dir, changed (dict[str, set[int]] of changed line numbers per file, from the already-existing changed_line_numbers())
functions.output: list[str] of error messages, one per changed DB/HTTP-touching function with no matching real-layer test and no exemption; empty list when clean
functions.if_none: Returns [] immediately if project_dir is falsy -- matches every other diff-scoped scanner's guard in this file

functions.name: _ast_functions
functions.input: source text of a Python file, its path (for AST error messages)
functions.output: list of {name, start, end, calls} dicts, one per function/method found via ast.walk -- calls is the set of bare local-name calls made in that function's body, used for the one-level call resolution
functions.if_none: Returns [] on a SyntaxError rather than raising -- a file that fails to parse is not this check's job to diagnose

break_it.scenario: A function delegates DB/HTTP work through more than one level of local helper calls (A calls B, B calls C, C is the one that touches the database) -- this check only resolves ONE level.
break_it.what_happens: A genuinely DB-touching change could pass this check unflagged if the delegation chain is 2+ helpers deep.
break_it.how: NOT mitigated -- deliberately scoped to one level, documented in _ast_functions' own docstring, because this repo's actual pattern (checked across 4 sampled files: drawdown_verify.py, lot_search.py, solar_yield.py, plus da_outcome.py/upzoning_check.py as negative controls) is a route/entry function calling a DIRECT local DB/HTTP helper, not deep chains. Named as a real, accepted limit rather than silently assumed away.
break_it.repro: N/A -- would need a real multi-level delegation example in this codebase to reproduce; not found in the files sampled this session

break_it.scenario: DB/HTTP calls hidden inside a module-level constant or a class attribute (not inside any function body) -- e.g. a PROBES-style dict of (sql, params) tuples used later by a generic runner, the exact shape scripts/dq_probe_live.py itself uses.
break_it.what_happens: A changed module-level data structure that effectively causes a DB query to run later would not be flagged, since this check only walks FunctionDef/AsyncFunctionDef bodies.
break_it.how: NOT mitigated -- named, not silently assumed away. Confirmed this session that scripts/dq_probe_live.py's own PROBES dict additions (module-level, not inside a function) would not trigger this check. Extending to module-level assignment scanning was considered and deliberately deferred: it meaningfully increases false-positive risk on legitimately data-only files and was not proven necessary against real examples in the time available this session.
break_it.repro: python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); import qa_gate; print(qa_gate.check_real_layer_test_exists({}, ['scripts/dq_probe_live.py'], '.', {'scripts/dq_probe_live.py': {1400}}))" -- returns [] even though PROBES dict entries do drive real queries

break_it.scenario: This check requires a test FILE to exist and carry the right marker, but never confirms the test actually EXERCISES the specific changed function -- a real_layer test file matching the naming convention but covering something else entirely in the same file would satisfy this check without proving anything about the actual change.
break_it.what_happens: A PR could pass this gate with a real-DB test file present that has nothing to do with the specific function that changed.
break_it.how: NOT mitigated. This layer answers 'does SOME real-layer test exist for this file', not 'does a real-layer test cover THIS function' -- the latter would need per-function test-to-code mapping, a meaningfully larger undertaking. Section 1's falsifiable_check.observed_red (already required, already enforced) is where the specific proof that the RIGHT test was run against the RIGHT function is meant to live -- this layer's job is narrower: make sure a candidate exists to run at all, which was the actual gap this session found (DQ-91: no real-layer test existed anywhere for the file in question).
break_it.repro: N/A -- a scope limitation, not a bug to reproduce

break_it.scenario: _REAL_DB_HTTP_TRIGGER_RE matches against a function's whole body text, including comments and docstrings -- not just executable code. Found for real, not hypothetically: pushing this exact commit made the gate fail against scripts/qa_gate.py itself, because _ast_functions' own docstring explained the drawdown_verify.py example using the literal text '.execute()' as prose, which the trigger regex cannot distinguish from a real call.
break_it.what_happens: A file whose comments/docstrings merely DESCRIBE or reference a DB/HTTP call pattern, without making one, gets flagged as if it made one -- a false positive, and specifically a self-referential one on this file, since it is the one file in the repo whose job is to explain what these patterns look like.
break_it.how: Mitigated for the one real instance found (reworded the docstring to describe the call without using the literal '.execute(' substring) rather than by suppressing the file. NOT mitigated at the mechanism level -- token-stripping comments/docstrings before matching (e.g. via the tokenize module) was considered and deliberately deferred: function-body text sliced by line range is not always independently tokenizable (inconsistent leading indentation on a method body can raise IndentationError), so a naive implementation trades one class of false positive for a different silent-miss failure mode, and this was not proven safe in the time available. Symmetric to the already-fixed _REAL_LAYER_MARK_RE comment-matching bug, on the trigger side instead of the marker side -- named so the next occurrence in some other file's docstring is recognised immediately rather than re-discovered.
break_it.repro: python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); import qa_gate; print(qa_gate.check_real_layer_test_exists({}, ['scripts/qa_gate.py'], '.', qa_gate.changed_line_numbers(['scripts/qa_gate.py'], '.').get('scripts/qa_gate.py', set())))" against a version of this file with a docstring containing the literal substring '.execute(' as prose -- reproduces the false positive that blocked this branch's own push

post_merge.manual_verify: No -- verified in-session by forcing the exact failure this check exists to catch (real test files hidden) against the real file/function that motivated it, watching it fail for the wrong reason once, fixing that, and re-verifying it fails for the right reason and passes when restored.
